correctness.rationale: With a leaders in A, b=k-a in B and followers p=m-a, q=m+1-b, block diagonalization gives J=p/(m+1)+q/m+(2m+1)pq/(m(m+1)(m(m+1)-pq)); positive determinant holds for nonempty follower set. For k<=m, J(a) lies strictly above the chord joining J(0) and J(k): a(k-a)(2m+1)(k(m+1)-a-1)/(k^2m(m+1)(km+a^2-ka+a))>0 for all 0<a<k, so no mixed optimizer. Endpoint difference J(k)-J(0)=(k^2-2m-1)/(k m(m+1)) proves the square-root threshold including odd-square ties. For larger k, the all-B configuration has q=0, and for any q>0 the difference is q(1/m-1/(m+1)) plus a nonnegative pq term, strictly positive. Orthogonality and within-part permutations yield exact counts. I independently checked the chord polynomial identity symbolically, exact rational optimization for all m=2..30 and all budgets 1..2m, including boundary cases.
residual_risks: No formal Lean proof; bounded independent calculations corroborate but are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The grounded trace is a canonical coherence cost and K_{m,m+1} a natural sharply near-balanced family. A closed optimizer count and exact square-root changeover from smaller to larger part, with rigorous exclusion of intermediate mixed sets and a provable nonnested optimum, provide a usable structural test family for leader-budget design. The exact switch and strict chord inequality are not a routine one-off graph evaluation.
residual_risks: All parameter computations m<=30 are consistency checks, not proof.

final_claim: For the unweighted K_{m,m+1}, m>=2, among exactly k noiseless leaders minimizing tr(L_FF^{-1}), if 1<=k<=m the optimal leaders all belong to smaller part A when k^2<2m+1, all belong to larger part B when k^2>2m+1, and precisely both pure classes tie when equality holds, with no mixed optimal set. For m+1<=k<=2m all of B and any k-m-1 of A are optimal. Every optimizer and binomial count is classified.
limitations: Unweighted exact two-part size difference one, row noiseless leaders, m>=2 and 1<=k<=2m.
No claim for arbitrarily unbalanced multipartite graphs or noisy finite-gain leaders.
All parameter computations m<=30 are consistency checks, not proof.
